result:
At dusk, the city loosens its grip on the day. Windows glow like small lanterns, and traffic becomes a river of red and white sparks. I carry a cup of tea to the roof, where the air smells of rain and warm stone. Above me, the first star appears, patient as a friend who knows I will eventually look up.

I used to think the sky was a distant ceiling, beautiful but unreachable. Now I imagine it as a library with no walls, each constellation a story pinned in darkness. Some stories are ancient beyond human memory; others are being written this minute, as satellites cross silently overhead and somewhere a child asks why the moon follows the car.

My cup cools between my hands. A neighbor laughs behind a wall, then a door closes. The sounds do not spoil the night; they give it scale. The universe is vast, but so is the kindness of someone holding an elevator, or remembering how you take your coffee. Perhaps wonder is not an escape from daily life. Perhaps it is the ability to notice that daily life is already astonishing.

Tonight, I make no wish on the star. I watch it shine through the haze, a pinprick of light traveling toward this roof. By the time it reaches me, its source may have changed, yet the message remains: keep looking, keep listening, keep making room for what you cannot explain. Then morning will come, bringing a quiet universe of beginnings.
